newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES SOFTER AGAINST UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES SOFTER AGAINST UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar finished Tuesday's interbank session easier against hard currencies on the back of continued import pressure, dealers said.
"The Zimbabwe dollar declined by about 0.4 percent today and some guys even started quoting wide -- some two points or so," a dealer said.
"The (central) Reserve Bank were checking right through the market, but we didn't see them come in," he added.
Dealers in the morning said the dollar was likely to continue on its downward slide until the commencement of the annual tobacco auctions in April, a major earner of foreign currency for the country.
"But as of now the import pressure is still pursuing," one said.
At Tuesday's close, the local unit was trading at 11.2400/2500 against the U.S. dollar, some four cents down from 11.2000/2100 on Monday.
Against the crosses, it ended at 17.8300/8500 from 17.8270/8550 versus sterling and was also quoted softer on the mark at 6.6700/6900 compared to 6.6080/6180 the previous day.
It was indicated at 2.5400/5600 from 2.5240/5400 against South Africa's rand.
